missing_spec_content.spec_text: The higher the thermal conductivity of a material the higher the rate of energy transfer by conduction across the material.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson never uses the term 'thermal conductivity' and never states this relationship. The nearest it gets is 'materials that conduct heat poorly slow down energy transfer' (keyPoints[3].content), which does not link higher thermal conductivity to a higher rate of energy transfer by conduction.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Students should be able to describe how the rate of cooling of a building is affected by the thickness and thermal conductivity of its walls.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson lists loft, double-glazing and cavity wall insulation. It never explains how wall thickness or wall thermal conductivity affects a building's rate of cooling.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Required practical activity 2 (physics only): investigate the effectiveness of different materials as thermal insulators and the factors that may affect the thermal insulation properties of a material.
missing_spec_content.why: The required practical is not mentioned. There is nothing on method, variables or the factors that affect how well a material insulates.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Investigate thermal conductivity using rods of different materials.
missing_spec_content.why: No investigation or comparison of thermal conductivity in different materials is included.

above_gcse.text: Regenerative braking in electric vehicles: normally, brake pads waste kinetic energy as heat. Instead, the motor runs backwards and acts as a generator.
above_gcse.why: The specification section asks only for ways of reducing unwanted transfers 'for example through lubrication and the use of thermal insulation'. A motor working as a generator relies on the generator effect, which is not part of this section. This topic gets a whole key point, a checkpoint and a tutor note calling it 'a favourite exam topic', so it may lead the student to over-prioritise it.

above_gcse.text: This is why a perpetual motion machine is impossible.
above_gcse.why: Perpetual motion machines are not required by the specification. Here they are made a key term, a write bullet, a revision card bullet and a common mistake.

above_gcse.text: Sankey diagrams must be drawn to scale. The width of each arrow shows the amount of energy. All the arrows must add up to the input.
above_gcse.why: Sankey diagrams are not required by this specification section. Presenting them as an exam requirement may mislead the student.

above_gcse.text: It still exists, just as low-grade heat in the surroundings.
above_gcse.why: 'Low-grade heat' is not a specification term (it also appears in checkpoints['2'].correctFeedback). The specification phrase is 'stored in less useful ways'.

factual_errors.text: Electrical resistance — the property of a material that turns electrical energy into heat
factual_errors.correction: Resistance is opposition to the flow of current (R = V/I). Heating of a resistor is a consequence of current flowing through it, not the definition of resistance.

Cooling a motor does not reduce the energy wasted. It only removes the thermal energy after it has already been dissipated. Wasted energy is reduced by lowering resistance (for example, better conductors) and by reducing friction (for example, lubricating bearings).

factual_errors.text: Energy is never created or destroyed. It is always transferred.
factual_errors.correction: Energy can be transferred usefully, stored or dissipated. It is not always transferred: it can also remain stored.

factual_errors.text: On every impact, some energy goes to the thermal store of the ball, floor and air. It goes as sound and heat.
factual_errors.correction: Sound is not a store. Energy is transferred by sound waves and then ends up in the thermal store of the surroundings. As written, this suggests energy enters the thermal store 'as sound'.

The checkpoints object has keys '0', '2' and '3' only, so the key point on useful and wasted energy transfers has no checkpoint testing it.
